implementation_notes: The component is a class holding a BehaviorSubject<State> (it replays the latest state to every new subscriber - the exact contract of the state stream) and a Subject<Event> for intents; handlers are registered per event type or expressed as a switch over the event record and write the next immutable record with OnNext. IObservable<T> itself lives in the BCL while the operators come from the System.Reactive package, and UI stacks (WPF, MAUI, Blazor, Avalonia) subscribe with Subscribe(...) or MVVM helpers; dispose subscriptions and complete or clear the subjects when the component is disposed.
pitfalls: A subject's observer side is not thread-safe by contract; serialize emissions (lock, Synchronize, or a single-threaded scheduler) or concurrent Dispatch tears the subscriber list.
Subscriptions must be disposed: a view that subscribes but never disposes stays alive through the subject (the classic WPF/MAUI leak).
BehaviorSubject replays its value to new subscribers, so one-shot effects (navigation, toasts) placed in the stream fire again for every new subscriber.
OnError and OnCompleted terminate the stream permanently - report failures as state values instead, or the component can never recover.

variants.name: BCL channels + async streams (no Rx dependency)
variants.idiom_name: Channel<Event> for intents + IAsyncEnumerable<State> as the state stream
variants.implementation_notes: With only the platform: System.Threading.Channels.Channel<Event> is the event queue (CreateUnbounded or CreateBounded with a FullMode, ReadAllAsync), one consumer task owns the reducer and publishes immutable state records into a second channel, and consumers read with await foreach (C# 8 async streams). A channel holds items, not 'the current state', so the current value is a property and giving a new subscriber immediate state means replaying one element on subscribe; choose this form when no reactive NuGet dependency is wanted and bounded capacity matters more than operator richness.
pitfalls: A channel stores events, not the current state: a new subscriber sees nothing until the next write - keep a separate State property or write the snapshot on subscribe.
Bounded channels block producers on WriteAsync while TryWrite silently drops; pick one policy explicitly and log drops, or telemetry disappears under load.
The consumer task owns the state; reading it through an unsynchronized field from the UI is a torn read - publish immutable records and assign once.
Completing the writer ends ReadAllAsync for every consumer; a component that can restart must create new channels instead of reusing a completed one.
